hypotheses.text: Overt craniofacial dysmorphism is penetrant in only approximately two-thirds of FBXO11-related disorder cases (ca. 60-67%) and can be subtle or clinically non-evident, rather than serving as an obligatory diagnostic hallmark across all affected cohorts.
hypotheses.rationale: Initial cohorts suggested distinct facial dysmorphisms in >75% of individuals, but recent expanded series indicate a lower frequency and milder presentation that leads to clinical under-recognition.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 previously unreported individuals with pathogenic or likely pathogenic FBXO11 variants, facial dysmorphism was documented in 67% of individuals.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.

evidence.text: In 12 affected individuals from 5 Chinese families with FBXO11 variants, characteristic dysmorphic malformations were not consistently observed across the cohort.

source.quote: Distinguishingly, malformation was not observed in all the affected individuals.

hypotheses.text: Seizures occur in 25-45% of FBXO11 variant carriers, representing a substantially more frequent neurological feature than described in initial index cohorts and functioning as an active discriminating sign.
hypotheses.rationale: Early series noted low seizure penetrance, but independent subsequent cohorts consistently report seizures in a significant minority to near-half of patients.

evidence.text: In an expanded international cohort of 21 patients with FBXO11 variants, seizures were identified in 43% of cases.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Microcephaly occurred in 24%, while seizures were present in 43%.

evidence.text: In a study of 12 individuals with FBXO11 variants across 5 Chinese families, seizures were confirmed in 3 of 12 patients (25%).

hypotheses.text: Increased body weight or obesity (HP:0001513) is a recurrent feature in FBXO11-related disorder that occurs in over 50% of specific cohorts, distinguishing it from syndromic intellectual disability entities characterized by growth failure or cachexia.
hypotheses.rationale: While short stature is frequently checked, several recent studies note increased weight/obesity as an unexpectedly prevalent metabolic finding in FBXO11-deficient patients.

evidence.text: Increased body weight was recorded in 7 out of 12 affected individuals from 5 Chinese families with FBXO11 pathogenic variants.

evidence.text: A 2-year-old female patient with a de novo FBXO11 c.1931A>G (p.Tyr644Cys) variant presented with obesity alongside global developmental delays and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Intellectual Developmental Disorder With Dysmorphic Facies And Behavioral Abnormalities
source.quote: The proband was a 2-year-old girl showing developmental delays in motor, language, and intellectual domains, strabismus, hypertelorism, hearing impairment, obesity, and brachymesophalangy of the fifth finger.

hypotheses.text: Nail hypoplasia (HP:0001792) and pear-shaped nose (HP:0000447) do not reliably exclude FBXO11 variants, as specific FBXO11 missense variants can directly phenocopy trichorhinophalangeal syndrome (TRPS).
hypotheses.rationale: Previous diagnostic guidance held that nail hypoplasia or bulbous pear-shaped noses distinguish Coffin-Siris or Koolen-de Vries/TRPS syndromes away from FBXO11, but case evidence demonstrates overlapping skeletal and ectodermal findings in FBXO11 cases.

evidence.text: A patient with a heterozygous FBXO11 variant (c.1781A>G; p.His594Arg) exhibited sparse hair, a bulbous pear-shaped nose, hypoplastic nails, and cone-shaped epiphyses resembling TRPS.

source.title: How many phenotypes for the FBXO11 related disease?
source.quote: These features include sparse hair, sparse lateral eyebrows, a bulbous pear shaped nose, a long philtrum, thin lips, small/hypoplastic nails, pes planovalgus; bilateral cone-shaped epiphyses at the proximal 5th phalanx

new_directions.question_text: Does the frequency of microcephaly (HP:0000252) versus macrocephaly (HP:0000256) differ by variant class (truncating loss-of-function vs missense) across pooled post-2018 FBXO11 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Goel et al. 2026 identified microcephaly in 24% of patients, whereas early publications reported normocephaly or mild relative macrocephaly, suggesting possible subphenotypic divergence.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of ophthalmologic defects (e.g. strabismus, reduced visual acuity) and hearing impairment in FBXO11 patients when evaluated by protocolized screening?
new_directions.rationale: Pan et al. 2024 reported reduced visual acuity in 4/12 patients and recent case reports note strabismus and hearing impairment, indicating sensory involvement may be under-ascertained.
